newsitem.title: USA: Arch sees positive free cash flow by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Arch sees positive free cash flow by 1998.

text.p: Arch Communications Group Inc said on Wednesday, based on the operating cash flow levels seen in 1996, it expects to begin funding its growth from continuing operations within two years

The paging company said its goal is to generate free cash flow, meaning EBITDA less capital expenditures, by the end of 1997 and positive free cash flow, EBITDA minus capital expenditures and debt service, by the end of 1998.

Arch posted fourth-quarter results Wednesday morning that included a net loss of $1.72 per share compared with a loss of $0.92 per share last year. Net revenues reached $86.6 million, up from $57.8 million last year.
Its fourth-quarter operating cash flow rose 43 percent to $30.3 million, compared with $21.2 million the same quarter a year ago.

Adding 218,000 net new subscriber paging units during the fourth quarter, Arch brought total units in service at the end of the year to 3,295,000, a 64 percent increase over the comparable period last year.
Arch also said it added 815,000 net new subscribers through internal growth in 1996.

C. Edward Baker Jr, Arch chairman and chief executive, said, "Despite a highly competitive environment (in 1996), we made substantial progress in assimilating our two acquisitions, USA Mobile and Westlink, and we boosted our annualized quarterly cash flow run rate from $85 million to more than $120 million."

For the year, revenues were $331.4 million, up 104 percent from $162.6 million in 1995. EBITDA climbed to $105.8 million from $47.2 million, and operating cash flow margin improved to 34.8 percent from 33.3 percent.
The company said the nationwide narrowband PCS network being developed by CONXUS Communications Inc for Arch is expected to be operational later this year.
